blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY— The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has released its long-awaited communication related to the US$100-million settlement between the Marinduque provincial government and Canadian-firm Barrick Gold Corporation over the 1995 Marcopper mine disaster that has polluted Marinduque waterways for decades, according to the Marinduque Council for Environmental Concerns (MACEC). In a Facebook post on Friday (Oct. 2), MACEC said a hard copy of the official DENR communication was released through lawyer Amelthon Sampayo, legal counsel of the original plaintiffs, and Rev. Fr. Arvin Anthony J. Madla, representing the environmental group. “Matapos ang mahabang panahon ng paghihintay, opisyal nang […]...
